terra.problem: The text does not say the Egyptians had been sure of themselves. It also does not call their knowing the LORD the whole point of His gaining honor.
The people speaking to Moses does not establish that they all stayed gathered or stayed put.
The text does not say Moses answers calmly.
The explanation presents checking a watch and standing calmly as the meanings of waiting and being still. The text does not say the people must stand calmly.
Saying Israel gets the day off adds something the passage does not say about their situation.
The text does not say nobody except God had a plan.
Dry ground does not establish that nobody had to slog through anything or that the ground was clean.
The comparison suggests the angel and cloud moved back so Israel could walk ahead. The text does not give that reason.
The passage does not say the ground stayed still.
The passage says the Egyptians had difficulty driving, but it does not say they had been driving fast.
The text does not say the drivers were fine before the wheels wobbled.
The explanation says the entire army of Pharaoh was covered without the text's qualification: the army that chased Israel into the sea.
The passage does not specify that the song starts on the shore.
The explanation repeats the answer without adding much meaning or personality. It is clearly flat.
The LORD tells Moses to lift his staff, but the passage does not explicitly say he lifted it. It says he stretched out his hand.
The passage does not say Israel's hands were still.
The song says more about the destination in verse 17, including the mountain of God's inheritance and His sanctuary. It is not all the song says.
The nap joke plays on the LORD's reign, making a statement about Him the target of the humor.
The text says Miriam took a tambourine and the women followed her with tambourines and dancing. It does not say she played before the others.
